hypotheses.statement: Lower volume ('we simply sold less') is driving the gross-margin decline (Sales director's view)
hypotheses.implication: Volume plans will not fix margin; group revenue rose 7.4% while margin fell 1.9 pp. Fresh and apparel did shrink, but that is mix, not volume.

hypotheses.statement: Mix shift towards low-margin electronics is the main driver of the decline
hypotheses.implication: The fix sits in electronics pricing and growth policy, not in cost cutting.

hypotheses.statement: Freight inflation from the March 2025 carrier contract is driving the gross-margin decline
hypotheses.implication: Freight (+€9M, +24%) is real but sits in operating costs; renegotiation is an EBIT lever, not a gross-margin lever (classification to confirm).

hypotheses.statement: Price/cost erosion within categories (rate effect) explains part of the decline
hypotheses.implication: Rates fell 0.5–1.0 pp in three of four categories, ~0.4 pp of the group decline; recoverable via promotion and terms discipline.

hypotheses.statement: Electronics is under-priced and can be repriced towards the main competitor without losing the volume
hypotheses.implication: Biggest single lever, but no elasticity evidence: needs a price test before committing the full gap.

hypotheses.statement: The 2026 budget (+25% electronics growth) will dilute gross margin further
hypotheses.implication: Without changing the growth policy, the 1.5 pp target becomes ~2.2 pp of levers.

hypotheses.statement: Freight inflation is an operating-cost (EBIT) issue that sits outside gross margin
hypotheses.implication: Freight renegotiation belongs in the EBIT plan, not in the 1.5 pp gross-margin count; confirm classification with Finance.
